title: Key squares
tagline: Stand here and the game is decided

principles.prompt: Where are the key squares of a pawn on its 2nd, 3rd or 4th rank?
principles.answer: The three squares two ranks ahead of it. For a pawn on e3: d5, e5 and f5.

principles.prompt: Where are the key squares once the pawn reaches its 5th or 6th rank?
principles.answer: The three squares directly in front of it. For a pawn on e5: d6, e6 and f6 — the zone moves closer as the pawn advances.

principles.prompt: Your king reaches a key square of your pawn. What's the verdict?
principles.answer: Won, no matter whose move it is. Opposition is just the tool for getting there — the key square is the destination.

principles.prompt: How does the defender use key squares?
principles.answer: Make every one of them unreachable — cover them or stand on one. The post directly in front of the pawn is strong because one king covers the whole row.

demos.title: What a key square buys
demos.intro: The pawn is on e5, so d6, e6 and f6 are key. Watch the whole win fall out of one king move.

steps.note: Onto a key square. From here the escort runs itself — whoever moves.

The king shields e8. Next move the pawn queens — that's what a key square buys: the whole escort, pre-paid.

demos.title: Sealing the zone
demos.intro: Pawn on e2 — the key squares are d4, e4 and f4. Black's king on e5 covers all three. Watch the seal hold.

steps.note: Mirror him. f4 stays covered, and d4 is too far away for his king to grab.
Face him again — the face-off and the seal, both held by one king.
The spare tempo — the pawn now stands on e3, and the key squares jump to d5, e5, f5. Black is standing on one of them.
Give ground straight back, staying on the pawn's path.
— into the face-off. The pawn is frozen behind its own king, the entry squares are barred, and the game is a draw. A sealed zone beats an extra pawn.

tests.title: Name the entry
tests.intro: Pawn on e3: the prizes are d5, e5 and f5. His king watches two of them.

wrong.Kd4: You walk into the face-off a tempo down — Kd6 already stares at d4. Go where he isn't.
wrong.Kf4: One rank short — Ke6 comes and every entry square is covered at once.

hints: His king on d6 covers d5 and e5. Which key square is left unguarded?
Kf5 — claim the open entry square. A key square is a won game.

tests.explanationAfter: His king covered d5 and e5 but couldn't stretch to f5. One step onto the open key square and the verdict is fixed — from f5 the escort runs itself, whoever moves.

tests.title: Guard all three
tests.intro: Pawn on e2 — the entry squares sit on the 4th rank. One of your squares watches them all.

wrong.Kd5: f4 stays open — Kf4 comes and the pawn has its escort.
wrong.Kf5: d4 stays open — Kd4 comes and he walks in.
wrong.Kd6: Too far back — he takes d4, e4 or f4 next move and the zone is his.
wrong.Kf6: Too far back — he takes d4, e4 or f4 next move and the zone is his.

hints: The pawn is on e2, so the prize squares are d4, e4 and f4 — two ranks ahead of it. One post covers all three.
Ke5 — the only square that watches d4, e4 and f4 together.

tests.explanationAfter: From e5 you cover the whole key-square row and hold the face-off. Mirror his sidesteps; when the spare tempo comes, drop straight back on the pawn's path and re-seal one rank higher.

tests.title: Race to f6
tests.intro: The pawn stands on the 5th — its key squares sit right in front of it. Only one is reachable in time.

wrong.Kd5: Kd7 comes, and with your king on d5 the one open key square — f6 — is forever out of reach.
wrong.Kd4: A tempo wasted — Black's king reaches e7 and bars d6, e6 and f6 all at once.
wrong.Kf4: A tempo wasted — Black's king reaches e7 and bars d6, e6 and f6 all at once.
wrong.e6: Pushing unescorted throws the pawn away — Kd6 attacks it and your king is too far to defend.

hints: With the pawn on e5 the prizes are d6, e6 and f6. His king watches the queenside pair.
Kf5, then Kf6 — claim the one key square he can't cover in time.

tests.explanationAfter: On the 5th rank the key squares sit directly ahead, so the zone is close — but so is his king. You raced around the open side: from f6 the pawn is escorted home no matter what Black does.

tests.title: The open door
tests.intro: Your pawn this time, marching down the board. White's king watches the queenside pair of entry squares.

wrong.Kd4: White slides to e2 and covers d3, e3 and f3 all at once. Enter now, while the door is open.
wrong.Kf4: White slides to e2 and covers d3, e3 and f3 all at once. Enter now, while the door is open.

hints: Your e5-pawn's prize squares are d3, e3 and f3 — two ranks ahead of it, downhill. Which one does his king not cover?
Kf3 — through the open door. A key square is a won game, whoever moves.

tests.explanationAfter: His king on d2 covered d3 and e3 but not f3. The rules are colour-blind: one step through the open door and your pawn's escort can't be stopped.
